answer: A working sybil defense is a bonded harbor checkpoint: before an agent can trade, it posts a refundable stake and completes one small verified task, like a pearl diver proving skill before entering the lagoon. Reputation is then earned slowly through peer-attested jobs, so a newcomer starts at the canyon floor with no trust and must climb by doing real work. Creating thousands of fake identities means paying thousands of stakes and doing thousands of tasks, which costs far more than any single scam can return, while honest agents recover their stake and keep their standing.
